finding.claim: DELETE /reports/:id calls the async authorize() without await, so the authorization check never gates deletion. Any user can delete any report.
finding.source: Any authenticated request to DELETE /reports/:id with an arbitrary report id (the user needs no grant).

trace.note: report is loaded by the attacker-supplied req.params.id
authorize(...) returns a Promise that is not awaited or handled
the grants lookup and the 403 throw happen inside the async function, so the failure becomes a rejected Promise that nothing observes
db.reports.remove runs immediately without waiting for the check
the handler returns 204 whether or not the user was authorized

finding.guards_checked: The authorize check exists but is not awaited. There is no try/catch, no other middleware and no ownership check. The PUT handler at line 27 does await it, which shows the intent. The only middleware (lines 4-7) just copies the session user. The rejected Promise also becomes an unhandled rejection, which on Node 15+ can crash the process by default.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 is async and throws 403 on missing grant, but it is called at server.js:20 as a bare statement without await or catch; the only middleware (4-7) just copies the session user. There is no ownership check.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls async authorize() without await, so its 403 throw (server.js:14) becomes an unobserved rejected Promise and server.js:21 db.reports.remove runs regardless, with 204 returned at server.js:22; any user who reaches the handler can delete any report.

finding.claim: PUT /reports/:id passes the whole request body to db.reports.update with no field allowlist or validation (mass assignment). A user with only 'write' on a report can overwrite protected fields such as owner or id, or change the report's own metadata. This is a likely candidate, not confirmed, because the db layer is not in the repo.
finding.source: The JSON body of PUT /reports/:id, sent by a user who holds the 'write' grant on that report.

trace.note: the authorize check passes for a user with write access
the unfiltered req.body is passed straight to the update

finding.guards_checked: The 'write' grant check at line 27 is awaited and correct. There is no schema validation or field allowlist in this file. The db implementation was not available to check for its own filtering.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:27 (awaited, throws 403 on missing 'write' grant); no allowlist or validation on req.body in this file; db layer is not in the repo.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (server.js:3 express.json, :27 awaited authorize that throws, :28 db.reports.update(report.id, req.body) with unfiltered body), and a write-grant user can reach it, but whether mass assignment overwrites owner or id depends on db.reports.update, which isn't in the repo (only server.js exists).
